Maintenance Report — MNT-0083-002

Asset: WELL-0083 (SW-24 Well 083, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 23 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 24 Dec 2022 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0083-0010 on 2022-12-22 Report written: 25 Dec 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0083-0010 at 08:45 on 2022-12-22 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.2% of the pad area, estimated 3.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 228 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 182 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0083-003

Asset: WELL-0083 (SW-24 Well 083, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 04 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 14 Feb 2023 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 244 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0083-0016 on 2023-02-02 Report written: 16 Feb 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0083-0016 showed the wellhead at 8.4 °C with the air at 7.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0083-010

Asset: WELL-0083 (SW-24 Well 083, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 08 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 24 Oct 2023 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 396 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0083-0051 on 2023-10-05 Report written: 25 Oct 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0083-0051 showed the wellhead at 26.1 °C with the air at 26.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0083-010 (WS-06).

  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 228 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 182 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0083-025 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.35% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0083-027

Asset: WELL-0083 (SW-24 Well 083, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 13 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 01 Oct 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 425 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0083-0146 on 2025-09-11 Report written: 03 Oct 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0083-0146 showed the wellhead at 30.0 °C with the air at 27.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0083-027; the manifest was only completed the following week (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0083-029

Asset: WELL-0083 (SW-24 Well 083, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Nov 2025 08:00 · Finished: 19 Nov 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 89 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0083-0155 on 2025-11-13 Report written: 20 Nov 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0083-0155 showed the wellhead at 14.3 °C with the air at 14.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 228 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 182 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0083-029 (WS-06).
